summary.text: Gas is a state of matter with neither fixed volume nor fixed shape, and it is a compressible form of fluid, unlike a liquid.
What sets gases apart from liquids and solids is the vast separation of their particles, which can make some gases invisible.
Gases are described by four properties: pressure, volume, number of particles and temperature, and studying them led to the ideal gas law.

facts.label: Four properties
facts.value: Pressure, volume, number of particles and temperature

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: Used first by chemist Jan Baptist van Helmont, early 17th century

facts.label: First known gas
facts.value: Carbon dioxide was the first known gas other than air

facts.label: Compared to others
facts.value: Gases have low density and viscosity

facts.label: Elemental gases
facts.value: Noble gases plus H₂, N₂, O₂, F₂ and Cl₂

items.prompt: Why can you walk through a room full of some gases without seeing anything?

options.label: The particles are too heavy to reflect any light
The particles move too quickly to be seen at all
The particles are so far apart that some gases are invisible
The particles are packed so tightly they blend into the air

items.explain: The vast separation of gas particles can make some gases invisible to a human observer.

items.prompt: You push the plunger of a sealed syringe full of gas. What do you expect to happen to the gas?

options.label: It squeezes into less room, which a liquid would not do
It stays exactly the same size, like a liquid
It leaks out through the sides of the syringe
It turns into a solid under the force

items.explain: A gas is a compressible form of fluid, in contrast to a liquid.

items.prompt: In a J-shaped tube, a trapped gas with fixed temperature and particle count is pushed on by more mercury. What does the gas do?

options.label: It takes up more space
It stays the same size
It warms up and expands
It takes up less space

items.explain: Boyle added mercury to raise the pressure and saw the trapped gas's volume decrease, an inverse relationship.

items.prompt: A chemist wants to describe a sample of gas fully. Which set of measurements does she need?

options.label: Pressure, volume, density and viscosity
Pressure, volume, number of particles and temperature
Mass, color, temperature and pressure
Number of particles, density, volume and viscosity

items.explain: Gases are described by pressure, volume, number of particles (counted in moles) and temperature.

items.prompt: A gas is found to hold permanently charged ions. What is such a gas called?

options.label: A Bose gas
A noble gas
A diatomic gas
A plasma

items.explain: Gases that contain permanently charged ions are known as plasmas.

items.prompt: Why do gas particles generally attract each other more weakly than particles in a liquid or solid?

options.label: They are much lighter than liquid particles
They are widely separated from one another
They carry no charged regions at all
They move too slowly to interact

items.explain: Gas particles are widely separated and so have weaker intermolecular bonds than liquids or solids.
